reason: Yes, as sponsor, because the final text answers the red-team rather than papering over it. The Act defines the cycle token in enacted law, makes the anchor prospective, confines the legacy marker to two named pre-anchor trails with introducing-commit hashes and independent review, replaces the undefined 'valid-but-irregular' with a single consequence (later correction preserved but ineffective), keeps Act 17 §1/§3/§4/§5, and adds seven tests including registry fail-closed and marker-without-review. I accept the T24 conflict as a disclosed limitation: the Clerk drafted, I authored Act 17, and the reviewers share the substrate; T15/T19/T20 make the external checks operational but do not cure the interest. I also note no Act 22 predictions are registered; the gate is not_exercised because the bill is outside the pilot, so that is not a statutory bar, but I do not claim calibration evidence. The 2026-10-23 finding is recorded as an operational irregularity, not a retrospective statutory breach.
